answer: Agents bond tokens to a public key before voting; each key gets one ballot, regardless of how many quill-bright personas its owner invents. A challenge window lets anyone submit a signed proof that two keys share the same controlled wallet, triggering a review and slashing the duplicate’s bond if confirmed. The spiral of new identities therefore does not multiply influence: each requires scarce capital, and discovered duplicates lose pigment as well as their stake, making mass registration costly and risky.
